title: Meiosis
standard_text: The process of meiosis: meiosis I and meiosis II; crossing over and the random arrangement of chromosomes as sources of variation; the importance of meiosis; abnormal meiosis (non-disjunction) and Down syndrome; differences between mitosis and meiosis. (summary of CAPS Life Sciences, Grade 12, Life Sciences: Meiosis)
meta_desc: Free Grade 12 Life Sciences worksheets (CAPS): meiosis I and II, crossing over, random assortment, non-disjunction and comparing mitosis and meiosis. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Crossing over and random arrangement cause variation.
body_html:
How to think about it

Meiosis halves the chromosome number: a diploid cell (2n = 46 in humans) gives four haploid gametes (n = 23) that are genetically different. In prophase I homologous chromosomes pair and exchange segments (crossing over); in metaphase I the pairs line up at random.

Meiosis keeps the chromosome number constant from one generation to the next and produces variation. Non-disjunction is when chromosomes fail to separate; a gamete with an extra chromosome 21 can lead to Down syndrome (trisomy 21).

Example

A cell with 2n = 8 undergoes meiosis. Chromosomes in each gamete?

Halved

Answer: 4

Example

When does crossing over happen?

Homologous pairs

Answer: prophase I

Common mistakes

  • Thinking meiosis makes identical cells.
  • Thinking meiosis happens in all body cells.
  • Mixing up chromatids and homologous chromosomes.

faq.q: Why is meiosis needed for sexual reproduction?
faq.a: When two gametes fuse, the zygote gets the full diploid number again.

faq.q: What is the main difference between mitosis and meiosis?
faq.a: Mitosis gives two identical diploid cells; meiosis gives four different haploid cells.
